topic: Lua state and scheduler negatives verification
title: Lua state global and coroutine API verification findings
scope: Follow-up verification for two open architecture questions: whether the client has a process-global lua_State* holder, and whether stripped Lua coroutine APIs exist anywhere outside the deferred event-condition scheduler.

processGlobalLuaState.summary: No process-global lua_State* holder was identified. The re-read 6A anchors still pass state through Component::Lua::GameEngine wrapper fields and call-frame wrappers: FUN_00CCF7D0 uses the LuaThreadInvokeState helper surface, FUN_00CF0910 returns this+0x2c, FUN_00CF09C0 replaces this+0x2c with a 0x140-byte frame, and FUN_00CF08F0 gates the active target at this+0x38. The loader bridge FUN_00D0FD70 uses resource/listener pointers and loader cache maintenance rather than a shared .data lua_State singleton.
basis: No `lua_State` debug string was present in the binary string scan.
No named stock state construction/destruction API strings were present.
The relevant 6A decompilation evidence shows object-relative fields and parameters, with no recovered shared holder referenced by both FUN_00CCF7D0 and FUN_00D0FD70.

coroutineApis.summary: The binary contains stripped stock Lua 5.1 coroutine API bodies and client wrappers, but the deferred event-condition scheduler still uses native C++ state machines rather than these API calls.

confirmedLuaCoroutineApiCalls.evidence: FUN_00DCFD30 references the stock `cannot resume` diagnostic and implements resume-state checks; FUN_00CF4230 calls FUN_00DCFD30(*param_1, param_2) and maps Lua error status values.
FUN_00DCF7D0 references the stock `attempt to yield across metamethod/C-call boundary` diagnostic and writes yield status/stack state; FUN_00CF38D0 calls FUN_00DCF7D0(*param_1, 0).

coroutineApis.deferredEventSchedulerConclusion: No event-condition scheduler function in the recovered chain (FUN_00897310, FUN_00897290, FUN_00896950, FUN_008955C0) calls the coroutine API bodies. The scheduler conclusion is narrowed to: deferred event continuation is native C++ state, while Lua coroutine support exists elsewhere in the binary.
